headline: Computational cost cuts enable long-read and population-scale genome assembly workflows
label: Scalable Genomic Analysis Tools
summary: Recent items report substantial compute reductions for nanopore assembly, telomere analysis, and population-scale pangenome preprocessing.
synthesis: The common thread across these items is reducing computational cost so that long-read and population-scale genomic workflows become practical. Embarrassingly_FASTA, a preprint, is a GPU-accelerated preprocessing pipeline on NVIDIA Parabricks that makes transient intermediates and spot-instance use viable, and reports cutting commercial genome processing from $100 to under $1 while enabling recomputable population-scale pangenomics. The published hifiasm (ONT) work produces near-telomere-to-telomere assemblies from standard nanopore simplex reads and reports a large reduction in compute. TARPON, a Nextflow pipeline, addresses downstream telomere analysis by isolating telomeric reads and defining subtelomere-to-telomere boundaries in Oxford Nanopore data. What is new is the GPU preprocessing design for transient intermediates and assembly from standard simplex reads. The thread is dominant rather than universal, since Embarrassingly_FASTA is preprocessing-oriented rather than assembly-oriented.
